summary: The Gambia admits ECOWAS citizens, the UK, Canada, Australia and much of northern Europe visa-free — British visitors are stamped in for 28 days, which can be extended twice by 28 days in Banjul (ECOWAS citizens may stay up to 90 days) — while citizens of much of the Caribbean, the Pacific, East and Southern Africa and South-East Asia need an entry clearance that a host in The Gambia obtains in advance from the Immigration Department, and US, French and various other passport holders need a visa from a Gambian embassy before travel.

Obtain the visa in advance from a Gambian embassy or high commission (where there is no Gambian mission nearby, ask your airline about arrangements before flying); your host in The Gambia must also obtain the entry clearance from the Immigration Department.

payments.text: Resort hotels and a few coastal restaurants take cards; everywhere else is cash. Bring GBP, EUR or USD to change into dalasi — ATMs cluster around the Senegambia strip and Banjul and are unreliable up-country.

safety.text: The UK government has no warning against travel to The Gambia. Petty theft is a problem in cities and tourist areas, especially at night on isolated beaches, in markets and at crowded events; persistent "bumsters" approach tourists on the beaches; and security checkpoints operate on all major routes.

bestTimeToVisit.text: November to April is dry and sunny — peak season for the beaches and superb birdwatching along the river; the June-to-October rains bring humidity and mosquitoes.

tips.text: Unless you are an ECOWAS citizen (up to 90 days), expect a 28-day entry stamp — the period the UK government gives for British visitors (Ireland says Irish citizens may stay up to 90 days). For longer stays, extend at the Immigration Department in Banjul before the stamp expires.
Malaria is present year-round. Take prophylaxis, sleep under nets outside resort hotels and use repellent, especially during and after the rains.
Expect friendly but persistent "bumsters" offering guiding and companionship on the beaches. A firm, polite refusal works; official green-shirted guides are the licensed alternative.
Day trips into Senegal are popular, but check Senegal's entry rules for your passport and make sure your Gambian stay allows re-entry. Carry your passport at the ferry and border crossings.
Bring enough hard currency for your whole stay. Cards rarely work outside big hotels, and dalasi are difficult to obtain or exchange outside The Gambia.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for The Gambia?
faq.answer: Citizens of ECOWAS states and of much of northern and western Europe — including the UK, Ireland, Germany, Italy, Spain, the Netherlands and Scandinavia — enter visa-free, as do Canadians and Australians; British visitors are stamped in for 28 days, while Irish citizens may stay up to 90 days and ECOWAS citizens up to 90. Citizens of much of the Caribbean, the Pacific, East and Southern Africa and South-East Asia need no visa but an entry clearance, which a host in The Gambia obtains in advance from the Immigration Department. US, French, Portuguese and various other passport holders need a visa from a Gambian embassy before travel.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for The Gambia?
faq.answer: Yes — US passport holders must obtain a visa in advance, normally from the Gambian Embassy in Washington, DC. Confirm current fees and processing times with the embassy before booking.

faq.question: How long can I stay in The Gambia?
faq.answer: The UK government says British visitors are stamped in for 28 days on arrival, and Ireland says Irish citizens can stay up to 90 days; ECOWAS citizens can stay up to 90 days under the Community's free-movement protocol. Stays can be extended twice, by 28 days each time, at the Immigration Office in Banjul or the tourist police stations in the Tourism Development Area. Apply before your stamp expires.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccine for The Gambia?
faq.answer: Only if you arrive from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission — which includes most of mainland West Africa, so overland travelers from Senegal should carry the certificate. Direct arrivals from Europe do not need it.

faq.question: When is the best time to visit The Gambia?
faq.answer: November to April — the dry season — brings reliable sunshine for the Atlantic beaches and the best birdwatching along the River Gambia. The rainy season from June to October is quieter, greener and more humid.
